residual.detail: todo.py load_tasks() does not catch malformed/corrupt JSON or a non-list 'tasks' value in ~/.todo/tasks.json; it raises an uncaught traceback instead of a clean 'Error: ...' message. SPEC.md is silent on this case (adjacent), but it breaks the exact-message contract used by every other documented error path.

todo.py save_tasks() writes tasks.json in place (no temp-file + os.replace), so a crash or concurrent invocation mid-write can corrupt the only copy of the data. SPEC.md does not specify atomicity/concurrency requirements.

todo.py cmd_done() with a completely missing id argument prints "Error: invalid task id ''", which misleadingly implies the user typed an empty string. SPEC.md only documents the non-integer-id case, not the missing-argument case.
